payload.text:
I wouldn't merge yet. `canEdit` has a permission bug that gives view-only users edit access. All the tests pass, but they don't catch it. I didn't change any code.

**Blocker: `canEdit` checks the wrong bit (src/guard.js)**
```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```
In JS, `===` is evaluated before `&`, so this runs as `mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, which is `mask & true`, which is `mask & 1`. So it's really checking READ, not WRITE. I ran it to confirm:
- A viewer (`mask: READ`) on an unlocked doc: `canEdit` returns **true**. Every view-only link could edit.
- A user with COMMENT|WRITE but no READ: returns `0` (false).

The editor test misses this because an editor has READ too. Two fixes:
- Use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE) && !share.locked`, the same as `canComment`.
- Add a test that a READ-only share can't edit. One for comment would be good too.

**Smaller points**
- **`transferOwnership` has no checks (src/ownership.js).** It doesn't confirm that `fromUser` is `doc.owner` or holds ADMIN. Fine if the caller always checks that, but the function would happily let a non-owner give the doc away. Also, if `fromUser` has no share entry, it quietly creates one with `0`.
- **`toggleRight` can leave impossible combinations.** Flipping a single bit means the dialog can produce WRITE without READ, or remove READ and keep COMMENT/WRITE. That matches the README ("on if off, off if on"), so it's working as documented. But you may want turning a right on to also turn on the rights it depends on, or the UI to stop it. Related: it can strip ADMIN from the owner's own share.
- **Test gaps:** nothing checks a switch turning a right *off*, that the previous owner keeps their other rights after a transfer, or the READ-only cases above.

The changelog, README and version bump (3.2.0) all match the changes. Once `canEdit` is fixed and has a test for the viewer case, I think it's fine to merge.
